ai.description: *Minervarya neilcoxi* is a small frog reaching 25–30 mm. It features a mottled brown dorsum with distinct longitudinal skin ridges and a pale, unmarked cream belly.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Minervarya neilcoxi* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, continuous, and well-defined light-colored vertebral stripe running along the center of its back.
ai.habitat: *Minervarya neilcoxi* inhabits moist deciduous forests and scrublands in the Western Ghats, typically found at elevations between 200 and 1,000 meters near seasonal water bodies.
ai.behavior: Neil Cox’s Burrowing Frog is primarily nocturnal, emerging from underground retreats during the rainy season to forage for small invertebrates on the forest floor.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Minervarya neilcoxi* breeds during the monsoon season, laying clutches of approximately 200–300 eggs in small, temporary rain-filled pools.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Minervarya neilcoxi* is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, primarily occurring in the states of Kerala and Tamil Nadu at elevations between 800 and 1,500 meters.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Minervarya neilcoxi* consists of a series of rapid, high-pitched, metallic chirps emitted by males calling from shallow, water-filled depressions.
